source.anchor: Original Samplinglib supplement: The weak forward equation from a martingale balance. Exact assumptions and formula below.
source.original_text:
Let P be a probability law on a measurable sample space and E a compact second-countable topological space with its Borel sigma algebra. Let X be a jointly measurable process on nonnegative time with values in E and continuous paths almost surely. Let g be a continuous real test, A a jointly continuous real field on time and state, and M a real martingale for a filtration on nonnegative time under P. Suppose that for each fixed t≥0, the increment g(X_t)−g(X_0) equals the time integral of A(v,X_v) plus M_t−M_0 almost surely. At every s≥0, the expectation of g(X_t) has derivative within the nonnegative half-line equal to the expectation of A(s,X_s).

The time parameter is nonnegative and the state space is compact, second-countable and Borel. The process is jointly measurable.
A single almost-sure path continuity statement holds for the whole nonnegative time domain.
The real test g is continuous, and the drift field A is jointly continuous in time and state.
M is a real martingale for the stated filtration and law. For each fixed t, the displayed pathwise increment identity holds almost surely at that t.

\left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_{t=s,\ t\geq0}\mathbb E_P[g(X_t)]=\mathbb E_P[A(s,X_s)]

theorem anonymous_target.{u_1,
    u_2}
  {Ω : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [TopologicalSpace E] [CompactSpace E] [SecondCountableTopology E]
  [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] (P : MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure Ω) (X : NNReal → Ω → E)
  (hX : Measurable (Function.uncurry X)) (hpaths : ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂↑P, Continuous fun t => X t ω) (g : E → ℝ)
  (hg : Continuous g) (A : NNReal → E → ℝ) (hA : Continuous (Function.uncurry A))
  {ℱ : MeasureTheory.Filtration NNReal inferInstance} {M : NNReal → Ω → ℝ} (hM : MeasureTheory.Martingale M ℱ ↑P)
  (hbalance :
    ∀ (t : NNReal),
      ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂↑P, g (X t ω) - g (X 0 ω) = (∫ (v : ℝ) in 0..↑t, A v.toNNReal (X v.toNNReal ω)) + (M t ω - M 0 ω))
  (s : NNReal) :
  HasDerivWithinAt (fun t => ∫ (ω : Ω), g (X t.toNNReal ω) ∂↑P) (∫ (ω : Ω), A s (X s ω) ∂↑P) (Set.Ici 0) ↑s

blind_reconstruction.text:
Probability measure P on measurable Omega; compact second-countable Borel topological space E; process X; continuous g:E→R; continuous A:[0,infinity)×E→R; filtration F and real martingale M.

X:[0,infinity)×Omega→E; M:[0,infinity)×Omega→R; s∈[0,infinity). The function to be differentiated has real argument t and uses t.toNNReal=max(t,0). E is not explicitly assumed Hausdorff or metrizable.

Assumptions: X is jointly measurable on [0,infinity)×Omega. For P-a.e. omega, X(·,omega) is continuous on the entire nonnegative half-line. g is continuous; A is jointly continuous. M is a true martingale for F and P. For every t≥0, P-a.e. omega: g(X(t,omega))-g(X(0,omega)) = ∫_{v=0}^{t} A(max(v,0),X(max(v,0),omega)) dv + M(t,omega)-M(0,omega).

Conclusion: Let Fexp(t)=∫_Omega g(X(max(t,0),omega)) dP(omega) for t∈R. Then HasDerivWithinAt(Fexp, ∫_Omega A(s,X(s,omega)) dP(omega), [0,infinity), s).

Quantifier order: For all listed data satisfying assumptions and every s≥0, the real expected-value function has the stated derivative within [0,infinity) at s. The balance hypothesis is for each t separately mu-a.e.; no common all-t full-measure balance event is assumed.

Scope: Derivative within the nonnegative real half-line at every s≥0, including the one-sided boundary s=0. No M(0)=0 requirement. No fixed finite horizon appears.

Constant dependencies: No existential constants; derivative value is determined by the supplied A,X,P,s.

import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.WeakDiffusionLaw
import Mathlib.Probability.Martingale.Basic

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.WeakMartingaleEvolution

open Filter MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Set
open scoped NNReal Topology
open AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.WeakProbabilityIntegral
open AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.WeakDiffusionLaw

/-- The expectation of a continuous test of a compact-state process satisfies
the weak forward derivative when its pathwise increment has a continuous
drift and a centered integrable residual. The residual may be chosen separately
at each horizon. At time zero the derivative is from the right. -/
theorem hasDerivWithinAt_expectation_of_centered_balance
    {Ω E : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [TopologicalSpace E] [CompactSpace E]
    [SecondCountableTopology E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    (P : ProbabilityMeasure Ω) (X : ℝ≥0 → Ω → E)
    (hX : Measurable (Function.uncurry X))
    (hpaths : ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : Measure Ω), Continuous (fun t => X t ω))
    (g : E → ℝ) (hg : Continuous g)
    (A : ℝ≥0 → E → ℝ) (hA : Continuous (Function.uncurry A))
    (hbalance : ∀ t : ℝ≥0, ∃ Z : Ω → ℝ, Integrable Z (P : Measure Ω) ∧
      (∫ ω, Z ω ∂(P : Measure Ω)) = 0 ∧
      (∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : Measure Ω), g (X t ω) - g (X 0 ω) =
        (∫ v in (0 : ℝ)..(t : ℝ), A v.toNNReal (X v.toNNReal ω)) + Z ω))
    (s : ℝ≥0) :
    HasDerivWithinAt (fun t : ℝ => ∫ ω, g (X t.toNNReal ω) ∂(P : Measure Ω))
      (∫ ω, A s (X s ω) ∂(P : Measure Ω)) (Ici 0) (s : ℝ) := by
  let Y (t : ℝ) := X t.toNNReal
  let A' (t : ℝ) := A t.toNNReal
  have hY (t : ℝ) : Measurable (Y t) :=
    hX.comp (measurable_const.prodMk measurable_id)
  have hYpair : Measurable (Function.uncurry Y) :=
    hX.comp ((continuous_real_toNNReal.measurable.comp measurable_fst).prodMk measurable_snd)
  have hYpaths : ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : Measure Ω), Continuous (fun t => Y t ω) :=
    hpaths.mono fun _ hω => hω.comp continuous_real_toNNReal
  have hA' : Continuous (Function.uncurry A') :=
    hA.comp ((continuous_real_toNNReal.comp continuous_fst).prodMk continuous_snd)
  have hAsection (t : ℝ) : Measurable (A' t) :=
    hA'.measurable.comp (measurable_const.prodMk measurable_id)
  let ν (t : ℝ) := P.map (hY t).aemeasurable
  have hν : Continuous ν := continuous_marginal_law_of_ae_continuous P Y hY hYpaths
  let F (t : ℝ) := ∫ ω, g (Y t ω) ∂(P : Measure Ω)
  let B (t : ℝ) := ∫ x, A' t x ∂(ν t : Measure E)
  have hB : Continuous B := continuous_integral_of_compact hA' hν
  have hmap (t : ℝ) {f : E → ℝ} (hf : Measurable f) :
      (∫ x, f x ∂(ν t : Measure E)) = ∫ ω, f (Y t ω) ∂(P : Measure Ω) := by
    rw [show (ν t : Measure E) = (P : Measure Ω).map (Y t) from ProbabilityMeasure.toMeasure_map ..]
    exact integral_map (hY t).aemeasurable hf.aestronglyMeasurable
  let gB := BoundedContinuousFunction.mkOfCompact ⟨g, hg⟩
  have hgi (t : ℝ) : Integrable (fun ω => g (Y t ω)) (P : Measure Ω) :=
    Integrable.of_bound (hg.measurable.comp (hY t)).aestronglyMeasurable ‖gB‖
      (ae_of_all _ fun ω => gB.norm_coe_le_norm (Y t ω))
  have hF (t : ℝ≥0) : F t = F 0 + ∫ v in (0 : ℝ)..(t : ℝ), B v := by
    let q := volume.restrict (uIoc (0 : ℝ) (t : ℝ))
    have : IsFiniteMeasure q := by
      apply isFiniteMeasure_restrict.2
      rw [Real.volume_uIoc]
      exact ENNReal.ofReal_ne_top
    have hcompact : IsCompact (uIcc (0 : ℝ) (t : ℝ) ×ˢ (univ : Set E)) :=
      isCompact_uIcc.prod isCompact_univ
    obtain ⟨C, hC⟩ := hcompact.bddAbove_image hA'.norm.continuousOn
    have hd : Integrable (Function.uncurry fun v ω => A' v (Y v ω)) (q.prod (P : Measure Ω)) := by
      have hm : Measurable (Function.uncurry fun v ω => A' v (Y v ω)) :=
        hA'.measurable.comp (measurable_fst.prodMk hYpair)
      apply Integrable.of_bound hm.aestronglyMeasurable C
      have hq : ∀ᵐ v ∂q, v ∈ uIoc (0 : ℝ) (t : ℝ) := ae_restrict_mem measurableSet_uIoc
      filter_upwards [Measure.quasiMeasurePreserving_fst.ae hq] with p hp
      exact hC ⟨(p.1, Y p.1 p.2), ⟨uIoc_subset_uIcc hp, mem_univ _⟩, rfl⟩
    obtain ⟨Z, hZi, hmean, hZ⟩ := hbalance t
    have hinc : ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : Measure Ω),
        g (Y t ω) - g (Y 0 ω) =
          (∫ v in (0 : ℝ)..(t : ℝ), A' v (Y v ω)) + Z ω := by
      simpa [Y, A'] using hZ
    have h := weak_integral_balance_of_centered_increment P Y hY hg.measurable hAsection
      0 (t : ℝ) (hgi 0) (hgi t) hd hZi hmean hinc
    rw [hmap _ hg.measurable, hmap _ hg.measurable] at h
    exact eq_add_of_sub_eq' h
  have hF' (t : ℝ) (ht : t ∈ Ici (0 : ℝ)) : F t = F 0 + ∫ v in 0..t, B v := by
    have h := hF t.toNNReal
    rwa [Real.coe_toNNReal t ht] at h
  have hD := intervalIntegral.integral_hasDerivAt_right (hB.intervalIntegrable 0 (s : ℝ))
    hB.stronglyMeasurable.stronglyMeasurableAtFilter hB.continuousAt
  have hderiv : HasDerivWithinAt F (B s) (Ici 0) (s : ℝ) :=
    (hD.const_add (F 0)).hasDerivWithinAt.congr hF' (hF' _ s.coe_nonneg)
  have hvalue : B s = ∫ ω, A s (X s ω) ∂(P : Measure Ω) := by
    rw [show B s = ∫ x, A' s x ∂(ν s : Measure E) from rfl, hmap _ (hAsection _)]
    simp [Y, A']
  rw [hvalue] at hderiv
  exact hderiv

/-- The expectation of a continuous test of a compact-state process satisfies
the weak forward derivative when its pathwise increment has a continuous
drift and the increment of a martingale. -/
theorem hasDerivWithinAt_expectation_of_martingale_balance
    {Ω E : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [TopologicalSpace E] [CompactSpace E]
    [SecondCountableTopology E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    (P : ProbabilityMeasure Ω) (X : ℝ≥0 → Ω → E)
    (hX : Measurable (Function.uncurry X))
    (hpaths : ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : Measure Ω), Continuous (fun t => X t ω))
    (g : E → ℝ) (hg : Continuous g)
    (A : ℝ≥0 → E → ℝ) (hA : Continuous (Function.uncurry A))
    {ℱ : Filtration ℝ≥0 (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace Ω)}
    {M : ℝ≥0 → Ω → ℝ} (hM : Martingale M ℱ (P : Measure Ω))
    (hbalance : ∀ t : ℝ≥0, ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : Measure Ω),
      g (X t ω) - g (X 0 ω) =
        (∫ v in (0 : ℝ)..(t : ℝ), A v.toNNReal (X v.toNNReal ω)) +
          (M t ω - M 0 ω))
    (s : ℝ≥0) :
    HasDerivWithinAt (fun t : ℝ => ∫ ω, g (X t.toNNReal ω) ∂(P : Measure Ω))
      (∫ ω, A s (X s ω) ∂(P : Measure Ω)) (Ici 0) (s : ℝ) := by
  refine hasDerivWithinAt_expectation_of_centered_balance P X hX hpaths g hg A hA ?_ s
  intro t
  have hMi := hM.integrable t
  have hM0 := hM.integrable 0
  refine ⟨fun ω => M t ω - M 0 ω, hMi.sub hM0, ?_, hbalance t⟩
  have hsame := hM.setIntegral_eq (show 0 ≤ t from bot_le) MeasurableSet.univ
  rw [Measure.restrict_univ] at hsame
  rw [integral_sub hMi hM0, hsame, sub_self]

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.WeakMartingaleEvolution

steps.title: Center the martingale increment
steps.text: Both martingale values are integrable and have the same expectation. Their difference therefore provides an integrable centered residual in the stated path balance.
steps.lean:
intro t
  have hMi := hM.integrable t
  have hM0 := hM.integrable 0
  refine ⟨fun ω => M t ω - M 0 ω, hMi.sub hM0, ?_, hbalance t⟩
  have hsame := hM.setIntegral_eq (show 0 ≤ t from bot_le) MeasurableSet.univ
  rw [Measure.restrict_univ] at hsame
  rw [integral_sub hMi hM0, hsame, sub_self]

steps.title: Apply the centered-balance derivative theorem
steps.text: The centered-balance theorem derives the integral balance by Fubini and differentiates the continuous expected drift. Apply it to the same process, test and drift observable.
steps.lean: refine hasDerivWithinAt_expectation_of_centered_balance P X hX hpaths g hg A hA ?_ s

lesson.lean_statement: Real-time evaluation uses the nonnegative part of the time. HasDerivWithinAt restricts the derivative to the nonnegative half-line.
lesson.lean_proof: After rewriting the observable in terms of its actual pushforward laws, the proof differentiates a continuous drift primitive and restricts the equality to nonnegative time.
